_about: Sourced facts only: what a rule says, where it was read, when, and what is not certain. No post copy lives here: the writer model writes every word the viewer reads. These 14 came from one research pass on 2026-10-05 (secondary sources). The harvest job replaces them with facts read from official feeds; the owner approves each one. status: checked = state with its source line; reported = state only with a REPORTED stamp.

facts.title: Two Working Days: Code On Wages And Employee's Final Settlement
facts.claim: Final wages are due within 2 working days of resigning or being removed. The clock starts on the last working day.
facts.law: Code on Wages 2019, section 17(2). In force since 21 Nov 2025.
facts.caveat: Covers wages only. Gratuity has its own 30 days.

facts.title: Gratuity: payment within 30 days
facts.claim: Gratuity must be paid within 30 days. It is separate from final wages.
facts.caveat: Reported in the same article as the 2-day wages rule. You need about 5 years of service; two High Courts accept 4 years and 240 days.

facts.title: 50% wage rule under the new Labour Codes
facts.claim: If allowances are more than 50% of your total pay, the extra is counted as wages. This raises the base for PF and gratuity.
facts.law: Code on Wages 2019, definition of wages.
facts.caveat: The ministry FAQ says take-home does not fall if PF stays on the ceiling.

facts.title: EPF wage ceiling goes from 15,000 to 25,000 rupees
facts.claim: The EPF wage ceiling goes from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 from 17 Sep 2026.
facts.caveat: Reported. The date is not in the gazette text the checker could open.

facts.title: EPF final withdrawal: 12 months wait
facts.claim: After you lose a job, the final EPF withdrawal waits 12 months. It used to wait 2 months. On a part withdrawal, 25% must stay in the account.
facts.caveat: Reported. The 36-month pension wait is not confirmed.

facts.title: EPF: 12% from you, 12% from the employer
facts.claim: You pay 12% of your wages into EPF and the employer pays 12%. The employer must deposit by the 15th of the next month.
facts.caveat: Reported. Source name to be confirmed.

facts.title: Zero income tax up to 12.75 lakh salary, FY 2026-27
facts.claim: In the new tax regime for FY 2026-27, a salary of up to ₹12.75 lakh pays zero income tax. The standard deduction is ₹75,000 and the rebate is ₹60,000.
facts.caveat: It is salary, not CTC. The rebate does not cover special-rate capital gains.

facts.title: Professional tax: a state tax, capped at 2,500 rupees a year
facts.claim: Professional tax is a state tax, capped at ₹2,500 a year. Delhi, Haryana, UP and Rajasthan do not charge it.
facts.law: State Acts. Odisha repealed it from 1 Apr 2026.
facts.caveat: Your state decides. Source name to be confirmed.

facts.title: Notice period is set by your contract
facts.claim: No central law fixes the notice period in a private job. Your contract fixes it.
facts.law: Delhi: one month's written notice after 3 months of service. Other states differ.

facts.title: Training bond: the amount must be a fair estimate of loss
facts.claim: A minimum-service bond can be valid, but the amount you pay for leaving early must be a fair estimate of the employer's real loss.
facts.source: Supreme Court, Vijaya Bank v. Narnaware
facts.caveat: The case was about a public sector bank.

facts.title: India has no right-to-disconnect law
facts.claim: India has no law that lets you ignore work messages after hours. A private member's bill was tabled in Dec 2025.
facts.law: A bill only. It is not law.

facts.title: Working hours: 9 a day, 48 a week
facts.claim: Delhi, Maharashtra and Karnataka cap work at 9 hours a day and 48 hours a week. Overtime is paid extra.
facts.law: State rules apply until states notify the new central rules.
facts.caveat: IT and ITES firms may be exempt in some states. Source name to be confirmed.

facts.title: An appointment letter is mandatory
facts.claim: The Labour Codes make an appointment letter mandatory, in a prescribed format.

facts.title: Variable pay and CTC structure are set by contract
facts.claim: Variable pay is contractual. Your employer cannot change a pay term without your consent.
facts.caveat: Read how your offer letter defines variable pay.

do_not_state: How long probation can last, or that a confirmation letter is required.
That notice-period buyout is legal or illegal.
That a company must give a relieving letter.
That a signed offer cannot be withdrawn.
That IT firms are exempt from working-hour limits.
Any figure, date or section number that is not in this file.
